Two routes, because the wave route that verified the other Banerjee tables has no power here -- every code appears at both waves. Mean within-family variance of p-correct is 0.01257 observed against a permutation null (4000 draws) of mean 0.04239 and MINIMUM 0.00974 -- the observed value falls below the null's minimum -- giving p = 0.0010. PARTIAL for two reasons: within a task family the items are interchangeable on this evidence, and no Haryana test instrument is deposited, so that Haryana used the identical printed form is inferred from the question numbering rather than shown. route: exact_reproduction (item x resp x wave cell counts) + published_scoring_denominators
evidence: STRONGEST ROUTE AVAILABLE, AND IT IS A REPRODUCTION RATHER THAN AN INFERENCE. The CC0 deposit (doi:10.7910/DVN/DIU6BU, one file, 'STOPTHEBURN Data.xlsx') is a REDCap export whose column HEADERS are the administered item wording and whose CELLS are the literal option labels, so both join axes come from level-1 source with no intermediate document. Every live item code is its header slugged mechanically: lowercase, apostrophes DELETED, every other non-alphanumeric run collapsed to '_'. That rule maps all 37 headers onto all 37 live codes bijectively with no residue on either side (the apostrophe rule is what distinguishes i_dont_really_care... from i_don_t_really_care...). Re-deriving resp from the cell labels and cross-tabulating item x resp x wave then reproduces the live table EXACTLY: 851 of 851 non-empty cells identical in count, zero discrepancies, with waves 0/1/2/3 read off the 'Event Name' column as Baseline / 1 month / 3 month / 6 month. THE REPRODUCTION ONLY CLOSES ONCE THE PERSONAL ACCOMPLISHMENT ITEMS ARE REVERSED. On the first pass 8 of 37 items disagreed, and disagreed as an exact mirror image (e.g. i_can_easily_create_a_relaxed_atmosphere: 20/27/59 at resp 0/1/2 predicted against 159/212/133 observed, and 133/212/159 at resp 4/5/6 against 59/27/20). Those 8 are precisely the MBI-HSS Personal Accomplishment subscale, which is positively worded; the live data has them reverse-coded so that high resp means more burnout on all 22 MBI items. With 6-x applied to exactly those 8, all 851 cells match. The shipped option_text-to-resp mapping is therefore reversed for those items ('Never' = 6, 'Every day' = 0) and native for the other 14. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF THE SUBSCALE SPLIT: the protocol paper's own cut-scores are depersonalization >10/30, emotional exhaustion >27/54 and personal accomplishment <33/48. At a 0-6 maximum those denominators are 5, 9 and 8 items, summing to 22 -- so the paper independently fixes PA at 8 items, matching the 8 the data reversed, and fixes the instrument as the 22-item MBI-HSS. The paper also states the PHQ-8 and GAD-7 'evaluate frequency of symptoms over the last 2 weeks', which corroborates the shipped instruction stems, and the deposit's own anchors independently encode a 14-day window in their day counts (0-1 / 2-6 / 7-11 / 12-14). A TRANSCRIPTION DETAIL WORTH THE LINE: the 'Not at all' anchor is spelled '(0-1 day)' throughout the PHQ-8 block and '(0-1 days)' throughout the GAD-7 block, with no mixing within either. That is two different REDCap field definitions, not a stray typo, so each section ships its own spelling verbatim. SCOPE OF THE VERIFICATION: it covers the item mapping and the option-to-resp mapping for all 37 items, including the 22 whose item_text is withheld on rights grounds -- the withholding is a publication decision and does not weaken the mapping proof. Item sets match at 37, resp sets match exactly (0-3 for the 15 PHQ-8/GAD-7 items, 0-6 for the 22 MBI items).

route: exact_reproduction (item x resp x wave cell counts) + derived_key_agreement + drag_index_resolution
evidence: THREE INDEPENDENT CHECKS, ALL IN verify_gilbert_meta_23.R, because this table admits all three. (A) MAPPING, BY REPRODUCTION. The CC BY 4.0 Mendeley deposit ships 'Assessment_Master File_Shared.xlsx' with per-item scores in Wave1_<n>Code / Wave2_<n>Code and a 'Data Layout' dictionary naming every variable. Live codes are those names with the wave prefix dropped and lowercased, and the live wave column carries what the prefix encoded. Re-deriving (item, resp, wave) reproduces the live table EXACTLY: 138 of 138 cells identical in count. ONE ITEM NEEDED A RULE, AND THE DICTIONARY NAMES IT: item 6 is scored 0-6 in Wave1_6Code because it has six blanks, and the live table carries the dichotomised Wave1_6Recode instead -- but its ROW COVERAGE still follows the raw column, because 72 rows carry a Recode value where the raw Code is missing and the live table excludes them. Both halves are needed: without the recode 14 cells differ and 6code carries resp 0-6, which the live table does not have; with the recode but the recode's own coverage the row total overshoots by exactly those 72. The control arm is reported in the run. (B) CONTENT, BY AGREEING WITH A KEY THE DATA ITSELF SUPPLIES. The spreadsheet also ships Wave1_<n>Response beside each score, so for every item the option that scores full credit is recoverable without reading the assessment at all, and no item is ambiguous (no response value ever scores both 0 and 1). The shipped item_text was transcribed independently from the deposit's 'Student Assessment Items.docx', whose 11 page images number the questions 1-38. The shipped correct_response then agrees with the data-derived key on 28 of 28 lettered items and on all four open-response items -- including item 13, where both the data and the transcription give a two-answer key (A and C, the numbers 7 and 4 among 7/2/4). A one-position misalignment anywhere in the transcription would break this, so it upgrades the number bridge from a naming convention to a content claim. It also independently reproduces item 6's dichotomisation: the only full-credit response string in the data is 56|57|58|60|62|63, which is exactly the six blanks in the transcribed grid 54, 55, _, _, _, 59, _, 61, _, _. (C) DRAG-AND-DROP KEYS. Six items (3, 4, 7, 25, 26, 34) store their key as 'DEST_i-SRC_j' rather than a letter. SRC_j indexes the on-screen list of draggable numbers, and that the indexing is ROW-MAJOR is an inference, so it was tested rather than assumed: on all six it resolves to the arithmetically correct answer, and on the four with a fully numeric source list it does so with no freedom at all (item 3 -> 13, 14 completing 9..18; item 4 -> 18, 19, 20 completing 17..20; item 7 -> 50, 100 completing the count by tens; item 25 -> 1 and 1, i.e. 1 ten + 1 one = 11, where the key points BOTH destinations at SRC_1). Item 26's source list is half pictures, so only its numeric half is checked (SRC_6 -> 40, which is 90 - 50); item 34's is 546, the first listed. THE DICTIONARY'S OWN WAVE STRUCTURE ALSO HOLDS: items 32-38 are labelled 'additional items added into post-test' and appear at wave 1 only in the live data, while 1-31 appear at both, with no exceptions in either direction. Item sets match at 38, resp sets at 0/1.

MAPPING IS DIRECT AND THE ONLY OPEN QUESTION IS WHICH FORM EACH CODE BELONGS TO. Live item codes ARE the source files' own variable names, so there is no rename to reconstruct (the single exception is the baseline typo wordpob4, which the deposit's own 07a_Student_Prep_Baseline.do line 208 renames to wordprob4). What needed testing is the form-to-wave assignment, because the live table pools two different test forms into waves 0 and 1. ROUTE: every code's observed waves must equal the set of forms whose variable list defines it. This is a prediction the data could refute and it holds with NO exceptions -- 37 of 37 codes agree, and 25 of them are form-exclusive, so the route is strongly discriminating rather than nominally satisfied: 17 codes appear at wave 0 only (the six listening_comp questions, objectid7-8, preposition1-3, and reading_level1_comp3-5 / reading_level2_comp3-5) and 8 at wave 1 only (listening_quest1-5, pronoun1-3). It also settles which wave is which: wave 0 is the baseline form and wave 1 the midline form, read off the data rather than assumed. SECOND ROUTE, CROSS-SOURCE AGREEMENT: the .dta variable labels and the separately printed instrument agree on the item wording for 49 of 49 item-form pairs. That matters because a variable label can be internal shorthand rather than administered wording (the bitew_2020_osss3 case), and here it demonstrably is not. The keys are the instrument's own explicit 'CORRECT ANSWER' lines, not IRW arithmetic. SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY: the verification covers the code-to-form-to-wave mapping for ALL codes, and the wording for the 25 codes that ship item_text. It does NOT rescue the 12 codes whose content differs between forms -- for those the finding IS that no single item text exists, which is why they ship blank. PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED for that reason.
